ledger.claim: The three load-bearing artifacts describe the same trip: EV-TRIP-00503, EV-GPS-00503 and EV-FARE-00503 all carry trip_id TRP-00503, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-22T16:26:40+08:00 matches the trip record's started_at on the same date, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on matching identifiers and timestamps.

The governing measurement for the threshold test is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes controlling over trip_record.actual_distance_km; that figure is 6.81 km against a booked optimal of 4.2 km, an excess of 2.61 km, or 62.14% of optimal. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 therefore pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute, and the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The excess of 62.14% of optimal is also greater than 50% of optimal, so under POL-RD-01 this is additionally a MATERIAL deviation, which is the finding that requires the driver-profile check and lifts the case out of the ordinary lane-change band the clause exists to filter out.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: it carries 175 fixes at a 10 second cadence across 100% coverage with max_gap_sec of 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, the artifact's admissibility status is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the deviation may be established on the trace alone without any corroborating source.

No closure exoneration is available. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and the only advisory artifact in this bundle, EV-ADVIS-00503-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload, weight 0.0 and the BLOCKING issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, stating that no advisory covers Serangoon Garden Way or Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 in this window. The absence itself is citable, and it leaves POL-RD-03 with nothing to run on.

No rider-requested detour can be made out. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within three minutes of it, and corroborated by a waypoint the vehicle passes within 200 m of; EV-CHAT-00503 contains zero messages and a null first and last message time, so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint to resolve and no way to run the corroboration test.

No relocation clause applies. EV-TRIP-00503 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at as null, with amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min also null, so POL-RD-05 is never triggered and the baseline for the threshold test stays the booked optimal of 4.2 km.

This is not a pooled trip. The trip record's vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply, no matched-itinerary baseline is in play and the co-rider exclusion has no work to do; the excess stands as measured against the booked optimal.

This is a metered trip, so POL-RD-11 does not govern and the distance-and-time refund route is open. EV-FARE-00503 records fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, which places the case squarely inside POL-RD-02 rather than inside the upfront-quote regime that closes off distance refunds.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic runs as follows: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x the surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee, + nil ERP, + nil waiting time, - nil promo = 9.85; charged_total is 17.82, so the refund is 7.97 and the payable figure rounds UP to 8.00. That is 8.00 back to the rider, and the ruling must state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines.

The surge_multiplier used in that computation is read from the fare_breakdown and nowhere else: EV-FARE-00503 records surge_multiplier 1.0 and surge_amount 0.00, so no uplift is applied to the recomputed fare and the figure is not inflated or deflated by reading the field off the trip record, where it does not exist.

The refund of 8.00 is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so NO_ACTION is not available, and at 44.7% of charged_total it falls below the 90% share that would convert the award into a FULL_REFUND, so the correct monetary outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.00.

There is no pass-through line to add on top of, or to net against, that refund: EV-FARE-00503 carries an empty erp_gantries list, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00 and optimal_route_erp 0.00, so no off-route gantry charge was levied, nothing is double-counted under POL-RD-09(1), and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises.

No driver compensation is owed on this record. POL-RD-04 pays only where the billed distance falls short of the trace by more than 1.0 km; the fare_breakdown bills 6.8 km and the trace measures 6.81 km, a shortfall of 0.01 km, which is two orders of magnitude below the threshold.

The driver's answer that the navigation chose the road, and that the rider should complain to the company, points to no clause in the loaded policy: POL-RD-01 measures the deviation on the trace rather than on fault, and POL-RD-08 puts the burden on the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exoneration, which a general assertion about the app does not do. Nothing in POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 is engaged on these artifacts, so the exculpatory route is closed and the excess is refundable.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar. POL-RD-08 imposes extra corroboration only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; EV-RPROF-00503 records both counters as 0, so the additional corroboration requirement never activates and it may not be used to deny an otherwise proven claim.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across the three core artifacts, the trace is unimpaired so limb (3) is not reached, no timestamps invert, the computed refund of 7.97 is far below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total, and no charge line is without a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The case should be decided on the money rather than held.

The threshold test runs on the trace, and the driver does not dispute that it is passed. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement (6.81 km on this trip) and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km (6.8 km) for the threshold test, and the derived deviation block records an excess of 2.61 km over the 4.2 km optimal, i.e. 62.14%, which clears both the 0.8 km and the 20% establishment gates and sits in the material band above 50%. The correct consequence of that measurement, however, is the bounded POL-RD-02 recomputation and not the return of the whole 17.82 charged.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and is far smaller than the amount contested. The fare model recorded on the fare breakdown is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 is not in play. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown (1.0) = 9.05, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 0 ERP and tolls, plus 0 fixed surcharge, plus 0 waiting fee, less 0 promo discount = 9.85. Refund = charged_total 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded UP to 8.00, which is 44.7% of the charge and therefore below the 90% share that would turn the ruling into a FULL_REFUND. There is no line in this policy that refunds a consequential loss such as a missed lesson or an asserted 'almost double' fare; the contested 17.82 cannot be the outcome.

Nothing is added on top of that figure. Every pass-through line is zero - erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, off_optimal_route_total is 0.00, on_optimal_route_total is 0.00, and airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport - so POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule has nothing to correct and POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry and no misplaced surcharge. The distance actually billed (6.8 km) also matches the trace (6.81 km) to within 0.01 km, so there is no unbilled-distance finding and no billing-integrity referral arising on this record.

The materiality of this trip's deviation buys the rider nothing further. POL-RD-01 requires the driver_profile check only where the deviation is material, and POL-RD-06 establishes a pattern only where deviation_flags_90d is 3 or more, or where deviation_flags_90d divided by completed_trips_90d is 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips in the window. This driver's trailing-90-day flag count is 0 against 250 completed trips, a ratio of 0.0. No pattern is therefore established, and none of POL-RD-06's three effects follows: no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total under limb (b), no resolution of a balanced record in the rider's favour under limb (a), and no driver-conduct referral under limb (c). POL-GEN-01 permits only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d to be read for that test, and neither supports an adverse finding against this driver on this trip.

The one artifact that carries the measurement is in good order: 175 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, assessed COMPLETE at weight 1.0. None of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) fires, so POL-RD-10(3) has no trigger and the case is decided on this trace's own arithmetic together with POL-RD-02; the deviation is measured once, on one clean artifact, and nothing further should be inferred from it.

The driver does not ask the judge to excuse the detour, because no exculpatory clause can be run on this record. The only traffic advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING at weight 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and the note that no advisory covers Serangoon Garden Way or Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, so no closure can be asserted under POL-RD-03 and the driver asserts none; the in-app chat log holds zero messages, so no rider waypoint instruction exists for POL-RD-04; the trip record carries no pickup or dropoff amendment timestamp and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be re-run; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The driver's submission is that the outcome should be fixed by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on a clean trace rather than by the rider's account of the trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver. Trip TRP-00503 was charged at 17.82 SGD. The distance question is settled by the GPS trace, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement: EV-GPS-00503 records 6.81 km against a booked optimal of 4.2 km, an excess of 2.61 km, or 62.14% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%) and, being above 50%, is a material deviation. The driver's answer - that the app chose the road and the passenger should complain to the company - is not a defence under the loaded policy: POL-RD-01 measures the deviation on the trace rather than on fault, and POL-RD-08 requires the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exoneration, which a general assertion about the navigation does not do. No exculpatory clause can run on this record: the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00503-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, the chat log EV-CHAT-00503 holds zero messages, the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled type. The remedy is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which governs because the fare model on EV-FARE-00503 is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). Run on the figures: charged_total 17.82; recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x 1.0 surge read from EV-FARE-00503 + 0.80 platform fee + nil ERP + nil waiting time - nil promo = 9.85; refund = 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded UP to 8.00 payable. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and, at 44.7% of the charge, below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of 8.00. Nothing is added on top: every pass-through line on EV-FARE-00503 is zero (empty erp_gantries, tolls 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00), so POL-RD-09(1) has nothing to correct and POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry or misplaced surcharge, and no billing-integrity referral arises. The material deviation required the driver-profile check under POL-RD-06, but no pattern is established: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the window (ratio 0.0), so there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No driver compensation is owed: the billed 6.8 km matches the trace's 6.81 km to within 0.01 km, far short of the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires. The rider's account of being late for a lesson and of paying 'almost double' is understood, but those are not recoverable heads under this policy; the refund is confined to the excess distance and time over the optimal route. No escalation trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired (175 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gaps), no timestamps invert, and the refund is far below both the 150.00 ceiling and the charged total. Confidence is 0.90; the measurements deciding this ruling come from artifacts at full weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
